rubric.evidence: Verified on 2026-11-27 against MDN Translator_and_Language_Detector_APIs (HTTP 200) and MDN LanguageDetector (HTTP 200): the shipped API exposes the global `LanguageDetector` interface (`LanguageDetector.availability()`, `LanguageDetector.create()`), NOT the obsolete `self.ai.languageDetector` namespace shown across lines 23 and 39-41 of this stub (`self.ai` appears zero times on MDN). Also line 23 inaccurately states 'Uses Gemini Nano' whereas LanguageDetector uses a dedicated compact language-detection model.
H1 'Language Detector API' matches Chrome 148 listing; declared ChromeStatus row links https://chromestatus.com/feature/6494349985841152; breadcrumb links /v148/.

Honest MDN redirect stub (exempt from reference-contract.json): MDN Translator_and_Language_Detector_APIs and the dedicated /Web/API/LanguageDetector interface page both return direct HTTP 200 with Concepts, Interfaces, Security considerations, Examples, Specifications, and Browser compatibility.

Clearly describes on-device language detection and `{ detectedLanguage, confidence }` results, but misleads developers by showing the removed `self.ai.languageDetector` entry point and attributing inference to Gemini Nano.

Inline snippets in the quick-reference table call `self.ai.languageDetector.availability()` and `self.ai.languageDetector.create()`, which fail in shipping Chrome where the entry point is global `LanguageDetector`.
Lists `availability()` states ('available', 'downloadable', 'unavailable' — missing 'downloading') and defers full cross-browser compatibility to MDN.

Live check on 2026-11-27: https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/API/Translator_and_Language_Detector_APIs returns direct HTTP 200 (and dedicated /Web/API/LanguageDetector also returns HTTP 200). All external anchors carry target='_blank' rel='noopener' and citations are directly linked.
Single <main>, single <h1>, sequential h2 headings, <header class='lede-block'>, and <footer class='byline'>. Minor legacy stub gap: .doc-table omits <caption> and <th scope='row'>.
Uses /public/styles.css with viewport meta; recorded desktop:ok and mobile:ok in responsive-support.json (agent-reviewed 1280x800 and 360x740 DPR3 screenshots on 2026-10-10).
